steps.input: mem = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC task-954e23ac: fill horizontal gaps and extend vertical strokes upward', content='For recurring task-954e23ac, each horizontal colored bar may contain internal 0-cell gaps between same-color runs. Fill those internal gaps so the bar is continuous from its leftmost to rightmost colored cell. For each such gap-column, extend the bar color upward from its row through zeros, stopping at the first already-nonzero cell in that column (do not overwrite it); if no blocker, continue to the top edge. Also extend existing vertical marker/object columns upward from their topmost cell through zeros until the first nonzero blocker or the top edge. Preserve all original cells, dimensions, and unrelated zeros. The gap-row itself is filled, and the vertical extension includes its source row. Demonstrations establish local column blocking, not whole-row blocking: in demo 3 a vertical at c1 crossed another horizontal bar on row 2 because that bar did not occupy c1; in demo 2 extensions stopped at occupied cells in their own columns. In the solved test, horizontal gaps at c3/c8 were filled; vertical lines from rows 2, 3, 6, 8, 11 extended upward in c3/c8 until same-column occupied cells; bottom markers at c3 and c8 extended upward into row 12. Common pitfall: do not forget to extend the topmost horizontal gap at row 2 all the way to rows 0-1 when its column is clear.', path='arc', global_=True); print(mem)
